To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the neural activation in expert musicians depends on the upper versus lower melodic position in the texture, with a greater activation for the processing of the melody over the accompaniment.

(1) the neural activation eliciting the processing of polyphony in trained pianists depends on the upper or lower position of the melody in the texture, (2) the processing of the harmonic structure of melody elicits greater activation than that of the harmonic structure in the accompaniment and (3) both effects involve the posterior cingulated cortex and precuneas, among other associative regions.

the auditory processing of melodic lines and of accompaniment in the context of polyphonic music, is modulated by both the position of the melody within the auditory scene and by the harmonic structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural correlates of the construction of complex auditory scenes and their relation with multimodal imagery.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the auditory scene is not just the auditory scene.

the auditory scene is the product of the brain’s attempt to organize the incoming auditory information, and that it is a mental representation which is constructed on the basis of a variety of sensory cues.
the processing of melody and accompaniments in polyphonic musical contexts involves a distributed network of brain areas, with the posterior cingulated cortex and the precuneus playing a key role.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
melody processing in a musical context, as opposed to melody processing in isolation, involves a more extensive and complex network of brain regions.

the posterior medial cortex, which is known to play a crucial role in the construction of multimodal sensory imagery, also plays a prominent role in the processing of auditory information, in relation to the construction of auditory scene representation.

melody processing in the upper texture voice is associated with a greater activation in the precuneus/posterior cingulate cortex than the processing of the lower texture voice, and that harmonic processing of melody and accompaniments in a polyphonic context is associated with a predominant activation in the precunues/posterior cingulated cortex.
The main takeaway from our work is that

auditory processing of music, even in a highly trained group of musicians, involves the construction of a mental representation of the auditory scene that is strongly dependent on the cognitive processing of melody and harmony.
the auditory scene can be seen as a multimodal scene in which auditory information is integrated with other sensory and motor modalities.
the auditory scene, in particular the processing of melody and accompaniments in polyphonic music, is a multimodal process involving both the sensory and the higher-order associative brain regions.
